critique: The screen sustains a strong dark-space palette with cyan, electric blue, magenta, and restrained yellow roles, and its angular panels and monospaced labels form a credible system. The planet is the main craft weakness: its soft, blurry green shapes and smooth gradient feel like an unfinished placeholder beside the precise linework, pixel stars, and sharp typography. Fine cyan orbital lines collide visually with the sphere edge and vary in opacity, while scattered star pixels are unevenly cropped around panels. The outlined second line of the title has fragile legibility, several micro-labels are too dim, and upgrade cards have slightly inconsistent accent frames and internal vertical alignment. The bottom card row sits extremely close to the viewport edge.
suggestion: Rebuild the planet with a deliberate surface vocabulary—clean vector landmasses, controlled atmospheric rim, consistent shadow falloff, and sharper orbital geometry—so it matches the UI's precision. Establish one stroke scale for orbits, panel outlines, dividers, and icon boxes; clip background particles cleanly behind content. Strengthen the outlined title fill or stroke for reliable contrast, raise secondary-text contrast, and place all three upgrade modules on one strict internal grid with identical icon, label, stat, and level baselines. Add a consistent bottom safe-area and unify card accent colors by semantic role rather than per-card decoration.
audit_note: Direct independent visual critique from the r0 screenshot and brief only; no generation notes, HTML, other critics, revisions, or scores were inspected.
